current.why: The highest-frequency pattern cluster in the curriculum. Layered BFS is what turns 'shortest path' from a graph-theory phrase into something you can write from memory under time pressure, and multi-source BFS is the variant most people discover too late.

exercises.name: Rotting Oranges
exercises.note: Every rotten cell starts in the queue at once. Trying it single-source first was the mistake worth making — it fails on the second rotten orange and the reason is obvious in hindsight.

exercises.name: Koko Eating Bananas
exercises.complexity: O(n log max) time, O(1) space
exercises.note: The array is not what gets searched — the candidate speeds are. Recognising that the answer space is monotonic is the whole problem.

exercises.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
exercises.note: Jumping the left pointer straight to lastSeen + 1 removes an inner loop most first attempts leave in.

exercises.name: Course Schedule
exercises.note: Cycle detection framed as a counting problem: if fewer than V nodes leave the queue, a cycle held some back.

challenges.title: Binary search — first occurrence
challenges.brief: Given a sorted array that may contain duplicates and a target value, return the index of the FIRST occurrence of the target, or -1 when it is absent. A plain binary search finds some occurrence; getting the first one requires continuing to search left after a hit.

challenges.title: Multi-source BFS — rotting oranges
challenges.brief: A grid holds 0 (empty), 1 (fresh orange) and 2 (rotten orange). Every minute, a rotten orange rots each fresh orange directly adjacent to it. Return the minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if some can never rot. Every rotten cell must enter the queue before the first step, not one at a time.

challenges.title: Sliding window — longest unique substring
challenges.brief: Return the length of the longest substring of s containing no repeated character. The window only ever grows from the right; the left edge jumps forward when a repeat appears, and it should jump — not crawl one position at a time.

reference.note: Long-form, real-time study sessions with no narration. Useful as a pacing reference: it shows what sustained unaided practice actually looks like, rather than an edited highlight of someone already knowing the answer.
